documents.unit: Office of Information Technology (MyCGU AI guidance)
documents.title: Guidance for Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the application of AI to CGU
documents.summary: A short university-wide guidance page that frames AI as unavoidable, lists six guiding principles, and announces a ChatGPT EDU license. It welcomes free AI tools if data privacy policies are followed. It sets no rules for coursework, assessment, disclosure or misconduct and links to other CGU policies instead.
documents.stance_why: The page says the "academic community is welcome to use the free versions of AI tools such as ChatGPT, Google Gemini, and Microsoft Copilot, as long as they are used in compliance with CGU data privacy policies", which is permission with a condition. It does not hand course decisions to instructors or set any ban, so permit fits better than delegates.

units.why: The opening says "ignoring AI isn’t just unrealistic—it could mean missing out", which welcomes engagement with AI as the default expectation. It is a rationale, so informs, and P02 (welcome AI by default) fits.
units.resolution_why: Coder A chose P44 (professional skill), coder B chose P02. The passage says only that ignoring AI is unrealistic and may mean missing out; it names no employer expectation or skill, so P44 does not fit. It welcomes engagement, so P02.
units.anchor: ignoring AI isn’t just unrealistic—it could mean missing out

units.why: The page "aims to provide high-level info, policy, and considerations for using AI effectively in teaching, learning and working at CGU". It states purpose and scope of the guidance, so P56.
units.anchor: high-level info, policy, and considerations for using AI effectively in teaching, learning and working

units.why: The text recognizes "the landscape is constantly evolving" and says "thoughtful engagement is the best path forward". It sets no review cycle or commitment to revise, so it is framework preamble (P56), not P54.
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded P54 with phase over-time, coder B coded P56 with phase general. The source says the landscape, not the policy, is evolving and promises no revision or review, so P54 (policy will be revisited) does not fit; P56 and phase general. unit_stance neutral: the passage recommends engagement, not use.
units.anchor: while the landscape is constantly evolving, thoughtful engagement is the best path forward

units.why: CGU says it will "explore and apply AI in ways that enhance teaching, learning, research, and institutional innovation", a statement of institutional purpose that welcomes AI, so P56.
units.resolution_why: Coders anchored adjacent sentences of the same paragraph (A: 'our approach to AI is thoughtful, purposeful, and aligned with the university’s mission'; B: 'explore and apply AI...'), both P56. A set actor admin and neutral, B set actor all and encourage. The sentence names the whole community as the one exploring AI and welcomes AI use, so actor all and encourage; kept B's more substantive anchor.
units.anchor: explore and apply AI in ways that enhance teaching, learning, research, and institutional innovation
units.frag_start: Claremont Graduate University leverages the collective

units.why: The strategy is "balancing innovation with ethical responsibility, and navigating challenges like cost and computing demands". It names no specific harm, so it is a framework statement (P56), not P53.
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded P53 (ethical concerns), coder B coded P56. The passage mentions ethical responsibility and cost generically and names no bias, harm or environmental cost, which P53 requires; P56. Actor all: the strategy is addressed to the whole academic community.
units.anchor: balancing innovation with ethical responsibility, and navigating challenges like cost and computing demands

units.why: Principle 1 says "People, not technology, must be at the center of our work", a principle of the institution-wide framework (P56) with a must modality.
units.anchor: People, not technology, must be at the center of our work

units.why: Principle 2 says the technology "must be easily accessible to people from diverse backgrounds to bridge accessibility gaps". Access is the content, so P51; the duty to make it accessible falls on the institution.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P51 and must. Coder A set actor admin, coder B set all. The sentence imposes a duty to make AI accessible, which only the institution can discharge, so admin.
units.anchor: must be easily accessible to people from diverse backgrounds to bridge accessibility gaps

units.why: Principle 3 says "Digital and information literacy is an essential part of a core education". It is a principle about education, not an employer expectation, so P56 rather than P44.
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded P44 (professional skill), coder B coded P56. The passage names literacy as part of core education and mentions no employers, professional use or teaching of AI use, so P44 does not fit; P56.
units.anchor: Digital and information literacy is an essential part of a core education

units.why: Principle 4 says "AI tools should enhance teaching and learning", a framework principle with should modality.
units.anchor: AI tools should enhance teaching and learning

units.why: Principle 5 says "Learning about technologies is an experiential, lifelong process", a framework principle, not a rule on use.
units.anchor: Learning about technologies is an experiential, lifelong process

units.why: Principle 6 says "AI research and development must be done responsibly". It governs AI work in research, so P62; it states no restriction on use, so neutral.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P62 and must. Coder A set unit_stance restrict, coder B neutral. The principle says only 'responsibly' and bans or limits nothing specific, so neutral.
units.anchor: AI research and development must be done responsibly

units.why: CGU "has acquired a ChatGPT EDU license" for its academic community. A university-provided licensed AI tool fits P17; the privacy claim is coded separately.
units.anchor: Claremont Graduate University has acquired a ChatGPT EDU license
units.policy: CGU provides its academic community with access to a ChatGPT EDU license for research, teaching, and productivity.

units.why: The license "offers enhanced security and privacy protections, ensuring that interactions with AI remain confidential and compliant with CGU policies". This is a data-privacy claim about a vetted tool, so P50, not P17 which is about provision.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P50. Coder A set unit_stance neutral, coder B encourage. The sentence describes a property of the licensed tool and does not itself recommend use, so neutral.
units.anchor: enhanced security and privacy protections, ensuring that interactions with AI remain confidential

units.why: The community "is welcome to use the free versions of AI tools such as ChatGPT, Google Gemini, and Microsoft Copilot, as long as they are used in compliance with CGU data privacy policies". The privacy condition is the operative content, so P50 over P02.
units.anchor: welcome to use the free versions of AI tools such as ChatGPT, Google Gemini

units.why: The page says the listed CGU policies "communicate the requirements and expectations of the CGU community" and lists the Appropriate Use of Computing, Academic Integrity and FERPA policies. This points readers to the institution-level framework (P56).
units.anchor: CGU policies communicate the requirements and expectations of the CGU community

documents.title: AI - Center for Academic & Faculty Excellence
documents.summary: A teaching-center resource page that offers faculty communities, webinars, a curated reading list and an OIT SharePoint about AI. It sets no rules for student work and no default stance for courses. Most of the text is a reference list of third-party articles.
documents.stance_why: CAFE "supports faculty and scholars in using AI to achieve excellence while maintaining academic integrity, ethical responsibility, and intellectual ownership" and curates AI resources for faculty. It welcomes AI use for faculty but does not hand any decision to instructors, so encourage rather than delegates.

units.why: CAFE "supports faculty and scholars in using AI to achieve excellence while maintaining academic integrity, ethical responsibility, and intellectual ownership". It states support for faculty learning and using AI, so P63.
units.anchor: supports faculty and scholars in using AI to achieve excellence while maintaining academic integrity

units.why: "Connect with other faculty to discuss AI, academics, and scholarship" offers a faculty community on AI, which is support for faculty learning (P63). The offer itself takes no position on AI use.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P63, may, before-course. Coder A set unit_stance neutral, coder B encourage. Inviting faculty to a discussion community takes no position on AI use, so neutral.
units.anchor: Connect with other faculty to discuss AI, academics, and scholarship

units.why: OIT's SharePoint "is designed for the CGU community to explore OpenAI capabilities and access technology-related resources". It is an information resource for learning about AI tools, not a tool the course provides, so P63 rather than P17.
units.resolution_why: Coder A coded P63, coder B P17. P17 covers a sanctioned AI tool (chatbot, licensed assistant); the source describes a SharePoint site of resources for exploring OpenAI capabilities, listed among CAFE's learning resources, so it is learning support (P63). The ChatGPT EDU license itself is coded P17 on the MyCGU page. Actor stays all because the source says 'CGU community'.
units.anchor: designed for the CGU community to explore OpenAI capabilities and access technology-related resources

units.why: CAFE offers "curated AI-related webinars that empower your teaching and deepen your learning", faculty development on AI, so P63. It is an invitation to access them, so may.
units.resolution_why: Both coders chose P63. Coder A set modality may, coder B informs. The sentence is an imperative invitation ('Access ...'), which permits and encourages use of the resource, so may.
units.anchor: curated AI-related webinars that empower your teaching and deepen your learning

units.why: The page describes a community resource list with "extensive resources for teaching writing in light of AI technology", including sample policy statements, detection, and help preparing courses. CAFE curates it as faculty learning support (P63). It describes a resource and sets no rule.
units.resolution_why: Coder A anchored the 'preparing courses and assessing students' clause and coded P59, coder B anchored 'extensive resources for teaching writing' and coded P63. Both point at the same sentence. It describes a curated reading list for faculty, not what instructors may or should do with AI, so P59 does not fit; P63.
units.anchor: extensive resources for teaching writing in light of AI technology

notes: No school or computing-unit AI policy found, per collect file. The CGU Standards of Academic Integrity page was not collected (empty), so misconduct rules are not coded; linked policies on the MyCGU page were not fetched. On the CAFE page, quoted passages (e.g. the quote on designing assessment around AI-generated text) and cited article titles in the reading list are third-party material and not coded as CGU policy.
